hints.title: Cross Product Turn Direction Consistency
hints.text: A polygon is strictly convex if and only if consecutive edge cross products maintain the exact same orientation (all positive or all negative).

hints.title: Evaluating Signed 2D Determinant
hints.text: For consecutive vertices a, b, c, calculate cross product (b[0] - a[0]) * (c[1] - b[1]) - (b[1] - a[1]) * (c[0] - b[0]).

hints.title: Tracking Sign Changes Across All Vertices
hints.text: Loop through all n points using modulo arithmetic. Compute 2D cross product. If non-zero, check whether it opposes the existing established orientation sign.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.notes: Optimal linear O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space computing cross products.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Checking interior angles with trigonometric functions produces floating point errors.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Integer determinant cross products avoid transcendental math functions.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should handle collinear adjacent vertices where cross product is zero.
